claims.claim: Performance necessarily drops whenever total_tiles modulo num_SMs is nonzero because the last wave idles many SMs.

evidence.observation: Physical SM count is not automatically the one-wave worker count; residency, concurrent work, tile durations, scheduling, and the remainder magnitude determine observed impact.

challenge.alternative: When N is divisible by M, N%M=0 means the final wave has zero active workers.
challenge.check: Apply Euclidean division N=qM+r and account for the r=0 case.
challenge.outcome: For r>0 the partial wave has r workers; for r=0 and N>0 the final wave is full, not empty.

claims.claim: In an equal-duration, one-tile-per-worker model, N tiles on M workers require ceil(N/M) waves and a nonzero remainder r=N%M makes the final partial wave use r workers.

evidence.locator: problem grid and persistent scheduling model
evidence.observation: The documented model treats launched grid IDs as work acquired by workers, consistent with the page's simplified wave arithmetic when its assumptions hold.

claims.claim: A static grid-stride schedule leaves remainder tiles on a few fixed SMs, while a non-persistent fixed grid has no dynamic block scheduling.

evidence.observation: CUDA schedules blocks onto available SMs; blockIdx-to-SM assignment is not fixed by a grid stride. Persistence changes repeated work acquisition, not whether the ordinary grid is dynamically scheduled by hardware.

claims.claim: CLC is hardware dynamic scheduling in which idle SMs grab tiles on demand.

evidence.observation: A designated thread asynchronously requests cancellation of an unspecified not-yet-started block/cluster and processes a successful response; SMs do not autonomously grab arbitrary tiles.

claims.claim: Persistent kernels use an SM-count grid, iterate over tiles, and have no wave boundary.

evidence.observation: Persistent launch size is a software choice and repeated work still terminates with a final subset; persistence does not guarantee one CTA per physical SM or removal of all tail behavior.

claims.claim: Raster order and swizzle patterns improve worker distribution.

evidence.observation: These are software coordinate transforms applied to work IDs; they can affect locality but do not create IDs or guarantee a more even worker-duration distribution.

claims.claim: A B200 has 142 SMs; for 150 tiles CLC turns a 142+8 two-wave launch into one persistent wave with all SMs busy and causes the tutorial's 86%-to-98% result.

evidence.observation: The author's Modal B200 has 148 SMs, v6 uses static persistence without CLC, overlap remains imperfect, and the 86.43%-to-97.96% cumulative step includes other pipeline changes.
CLC cannot turn eight independent IDs into 142 or 148 independent pieces of work.

claims.claim: Tail effects are significant only for tile counts below four times the SM count.

evidence.observation: No four-wave cutoff is defined; impact depends on remainder, wave duration, residency, imbalance, and whole-kernel fraction.

challenge.alternative: The absolute last-wave cost grows with problem size, so it is not amortized.
challenge.check: For equal-duration work, divide at most one partial-wave duration by q full waves plus the final wave.
challenge.outcome: The fractional contribution is bounded by roughly one over the number of waves and shrinks as q grows, under the simplified assumptions.

claims.claim: For equal-duration independent tiles and fixed worker capacity, a single final partial wave is fractionally amortized as the number of full waves becomes large.

evidence.observation: The scheduler model supports the independent-work assumptions; the amortization follows directly from the wave-count arithmetic and is explicitly scoped.

claims.claim: CLC is available only on SM100 datacenter GPUs.

evidence.observation: The instruction requires sm_100 or higher and its multicast qualifier explicitly supports sm_120a and the SM120 family.

commands: Audit wave arithmetic and CUDA block scheduling
Inspect PTX/CUDA CLC semantics and targets
residual_risk: No GPU trace was available; the equal-duration model is analytical and real duration/residency must be measured.
